lines.text: Someone is still in there. That's the last line in the log. Oakhaven. Day eighteen. The checkpoint won. Seven votes. Steve, Caleb, Francis and Officer Reyes went in quiet. The soldiers who guarded that barrier turned at their posts, still in their helmets and body armor. Shots just bounce off. So the squad had to get close. And the families the Army turned away in the first days never left. They're still sitting in a mile of stalled cars at the gate. Dead. Reyes leaned too close to one window, and a hand came through it. Steve pulled him back out, and his shoulder came out with him. Francis caught a sheet of broken glass. Both of them are on cots tonight. They came home with sixty-six rounds, food, and medicine. And a clipboard. The clipboard was the checkpoint's radio log. Every message the soldiers got from the fort, written down by hand. Day one. The fort ordered them to turn every civilian away at the barrier. Day three. The fort called them back inside. The gate would close at six that night. Day four, one line. The gate did not open. The soldiers were locked out with everyone else. Then, at the bottom of the page, in different handwriting, not a soldier's. Smoke in the motor pool again tonight. Someone is still in there. Someone inside the fort is still alive. Asa drew a map to Millbrook on the back of a laundromat price list. Sixty miles of road. He didn't mark a single town along the way. Just one thing, circled three times, at the very end. An axe. Forty-three of us. Food for two days. Water for one. The horde reaches the fence in three days. Steve's shoulder might not be ready. Where do we go tomorrow? The fire truck, with Frost, for the rest of the water. Weston's greenhouse. Or the harvest, before the frost. Comment your name and your job, to move in.
